interpolation.group: ss~ annihilation processes (flavor-degenerate with dd~ and uu~)
interpolation.motivation: s s~ has identical dynamics to d d~ (both massless, weak isospin T3 = -1/2). With d d~ and u u~ variants in training for every topology, the network must learn that matrix elements depend on quark charges and isospin, not flavor identity. The most fundamental test of flavor symmetry generalization.

interpolation.group: Muon final states from bb~ annihilation
interpolation.motivation: mu and e are both effectively massless with identical EW couplings (lepton universality). With the electron variant from bb~ in training, the network tests lepton universality. Focusing on bb~ provides a richer test than light-quark initial states due to the b quark mass and Yukawa coupling.

interpolation.group: g+s processes from gluon + light-quark families
interpolation.motivation: With g+d and g+u in training, g+s is redundant since s is degenerate with d (same mass, same isospin). Tests gluon-quark sector flavor generalization. Only the quark (not antiquark) sector is held out; the antiquark sector tests the same physics.
b+d(~) and b+u(~) remain in training. Since s(~) is degenerate with d(~), b+s scattering should be directly interpolatable. Tests flavor generalization when one initial-state quark is massive.
c+d~ and c+s~ (same isospin) are in training; c+u~ differs only in the light quark's isospin (T3 = +1/2 vs -1/2). Tests whether the network interpolates the correct Z/gamma coupling across isospin.

interpolation.group: ds and s~s~ from same-sign light quark families
interpolation.motivation: d s scattering is intermediate between dd and us in flavor space; s~s~ is the CP conjugate of ss. With the other family members in training, these are straightforward interpolations. Tests same-sign quark scattering and CP symmetry generalization.

extrapolation.motivation: Multi-Higgs final states uniquely probe the triple-Higgs self-coupling vertex (lambda_hhh). Removing ALL such processes means the network has never seen this vertex topology. Includes the unique bb~ > hhh (only triple-Higgs process). Pure extrapolation of the Higgs potential structure.
The only processes with same-sign W pairs. Triple-W involves WWWW quartic gauge couplings not testable with W+W- pair production. Unique charge topology makes this pure extrapolation.

No ZZZ or ZZZZ vertex exists in the SM. ZZZ proceeds only through Higgs-mediated diagrams and longitudinal Z scattering. Qualitatively distinct from ZZ production. Tests extrapolation of neutral boson sector.

These uniquely probe the Higgs-tau-tau Yukawa coupling. Tau is the only lepton with non-zero Yukawa (m_tau = 1.777 GeV). Without these, the network must extrapolate the Yukawa vertex from Higgs with other particles and tau pairs without Higgs.

extrapolation.group: gg -> tt~ + boson (ttX via gluon fusion)
extrapolation.motivation: Combines heaviest quark pair with boson radiation from pure-QCD initial state. gg -> tt~h is the primary channel for top Yukawa measurement. With gg -> tt~ in training, the network must extrapolate the boson radiation pattern from gluon fusion.

extrapolation.group: gg -> W + qq' (W production from gluon fusion)
extrapolation.motivation: Gluons cannot couple to W directly. These proceed through quark-mediated topologies combining QCD pair production with charged-current weak decay. Unique interference between top-mediated and light-quark-mediated diagrams.

The ONLY 2->1 processes in the catalog: 1-body final state with zero transverse momentum and fixed invariant mass. Fundamentally different phase space dimensionality from all 2->2 and 2->3 training processes. Includes bb~ -> h (Yukawa-initiated scalar production).

The only same-sign processes combining two DIFFERENT massive quarks (m_c = 1.55 GeV, m_b = 4.7 GeV). Unique initial-state mass asymmetry. Includes novel topologies like cb -> st via W exchange. No other training process has this combination of initial-state masses.
